# HarnessDock v0.2.1

HarnessDock v0.2.1 is the corrected Tauri 2 release cut. It supersedes the incomplete v0.2.0 publication path, which could expose a release before the complete Tauri candidate matrix had finished.

## What changed

- Promotes the post-PR #47 Tauri integration fixes that were not included in the original `main` merge.
- Aligns the repository, all workspace packages, Tauri configuration, Rust crate and runtime metadata on `0.2.1`.
- Replaces the legacy Electron release path with an exact Tauri candidate publisher.
- Windows x64 Tauri packages contain the Windows x64 runtime only; Linux/macOS native optional dependencies are excluded from the Windows candidate.
- The legacy thin first-launch resolver is also fixed to honor npm `os`/`cpu` constraints before downloading packages, so a Windows thin runtime does not download Linux-only native dependencies.
- Thin first-launch progress now uses the same real package-download percentage shown in the status text; metadata resolution and runtime startup use a clear indeterminate state instead of a synthetic percentage.
- Thin splash rendering now uses the real HarnessDock application icon, fixed-size DPI-safe layout elements, and enough vertical space for first-launch guidance instead of compressing the icon/progress bar.
- Linux runtime preparation is explicitly glibc-only: musl Koffi/sharp variants are pruned before packaging.
- Linux AppImage packaging pins `linuxdeploy` `1-alpha-20251107-1` by SHA256. That release correctly skips RPATH patching for static ELF helpers, so DeepSeek Harness `landlock-run` remains available without breaking AppImage bundling.
- Requires the release workflow to reference a successful `tauri-candidate` run built from the exact same `main` SHA.
- Refuses to overwrite an existing `v0.2.1` tag or release and creates the tag only after candidate validation and asset assembly succeed.
- Removes the temporary AppImage diagnostic workflow after its fix was proven and keeps normal CI focused on source/test/Tauri validation.
- Keeps DeepSeek Harness pinned to `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1` at commit `cd5ef8148158c3a752a658978873241fdf8e2bbc`.

## Runtime and platform behavior

The public v0.2.1 assets are Tauri-native. Legacy Electron thin/full installers are not published as v0.2.1 release assets. The retained thin code path is still platform-correct for source/developer use and older-channel compatibility.

- Windows x64: Windows runtime only; no Linux Landlock/Koffi/sharp native packages.
- Linux x64: glibc runtime only; musl variants are removed, while the Linux Landlock sandbox helper is preserved.
- macOS x64 / arm64: runtime is prepared for the matching macOS CPU architecture only.
- Android and iOS builds remain platform-specific mobile candidates.

## Validation matrix

The release candidate must complete all of the following before publication:

- Windows x64 Tauri NSIS bundle.
- Linux x64 Tauri `.deb` and AppImage bundles.
- macOS Intel x64 Tauri DMG.
- macOS Apple Silicon arm64 Tauri DMG.
- Android arm64 debug APK and AAB.
- iOS arm64 Simulator application archive.
- Official pinned DeepSeek Harness source-pack build.
- Prepared runtime bundles for Windows x64, Linux x64, macOS x64 and macOS arm64 with platform-isolation gates.
- Runtime smoke tests with the embedded HarnessDock client.
- Repository/workspace/Tauri/Rust version-consistency gates.

## Release assets

A successful v0.2.1 publication contains:

- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-windows-x64-setup.exe`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-linux-x64.deb`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-linux-x64.AppImage`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-macos-x64.dmg`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-macos-arm64.dmg`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-android-arm64-debug.apk`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-android-arm64-debug.aab`
- `HarnessDock-0.2.1-ios-arm64-simulator.zip`
- Four pinned DeepSeek Harness runtime bundles.
- `SHA256SUMS` covering all published assets.

## Signing status

The public CI currently produces build-verified packages without Windows Authenticode signing, Apple Developer ID notarization, Google Play signing, or App Store/TestFlight provisioning. Android and iOS artifacts therefore remain developer-preview distribution assets.
